html:
SMTO-FIL-0029 — A file action on the Gateway took too long

GUID: 2a3f288f-f585-4c11-8532-d25d76a4aab6
Slug: file-timeout
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO gave up on a file action on the Gateway computer because it didn't finish in time. It may have been waiting for another change to the same files, or there was too much to go through.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether another Task is still changing files on the same Gateway computer, and let it finish or stop it first. Only one change can touch the same files at a time, and this action ran out of time waiting for its turn.
  2. Ask SMTO to work on a smaller part, such as one folder instead of a whole drive, or a few files at a time. Large searches, comparisons and listings can't finish inside the time limit for a single file action.
  3. Make sure the drive or network folder holding the files is connected and responding on the Gateway computer. A slow or disconnected drive makes file actions stall until they time out.
  4. If SMTO was changing files, open the failed step in the conversation and check which files were already changed before asking again. Some changes may have been made before time ran out, and repeating them blindly could apply them twice.

What success looks like

  • The file action finishes and its result appears in the conversation without a timeout message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Changing the Model's time limits won't help, because file actions have their own limit. Don't ask anyone to loosen SMTO's folder or permission checks to push a bigger job through; split the work instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway File operation raised timeout: the request deadline (timeout_seconds, default 30 s, maximum 120 s) passed at a cooperative check, the diff or ripgrep worker overran it, or the Files mutation lock (30 s for transfers) could not be acquired in time.

What this means

  • A file deadline/TimeoutError, bounded diff/search subprocess timeout or mutation-lock acquisition timeout prevented completion. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A file deadline/TimeoutError, bounded diff/search subprocess timeout or mutation-lock acquisition timeout prevented completion.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify lock-wait versus active processing and inspect partial/effect receipts before reducing scope.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway log for the operation and for another File mutation or transfer holding the files resource lock on the same paths. Narrow the scope (path, include patterns, max_entries_scanned) or raise the request's timeout_seconds within its 1-120 s limit, and check storage latency on the Gateway host; model/provider timeouts do not apply. Review the receipt's changes and residue before repeating a mutating call.
  • Reduce the file operation scope and inspect target storage health. Model timeouts do not control file operations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The relevant owner is settled and a supported bounded operation completes within its own deadline.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
